reviews.text: As of writing, I have ~10 hours and around 50/50 of them playing/afking. I have completed the entire campaign so far, which is 16 maps & a quickplay level. I am yet to try survival or co-op. As of right now I dont think the game is worth it. [h1]Pros[/h1] As of right now, the only positive thing I can say is that it has potential. [h1]Cons[/h1] [olist] [*] The biggest issue with the game is the limited inventory. Quite frankly, I do not understand what this is supposed to achieve. You are only allowed to take 8 towers in each level, out of around 40, and 2 power ups, out of around 10. However, you choose your loadout before you actually enter the level, so you have no idea what the layout or enemies are going to be. In the campaign so far, this isnt really an issue, because most of the towers are locked and you have to unlock them by completing the campaign. However in quick play, you have access to all towers & there is nothing more annoying than entering a level and finding out you need to swap your towers in order to complete it. There is no skill or knowledge in this, its just a complete waste of time forcing you to go back to the menu. A TD game is already about building the right tower at the right time, imposing a massive restriction on the towers is not only a complete waste of time, it also makes the game way more boring. There is no reason for this mechanic to exist. [*] The generator mechanic. Generators are blocks that produce resources at the start of every round. To activate a generator, you need to have it connected to the active ground, which is fine & to build anything next to it, which is just pointless. This basically means you have to connect the blocks to generators as fast as possible and then place a portable generator tower next to the main generator. This is just not interesting. [*] Game speed. This is maybe more subjective, but I personally find the base speed too slow and the fast speed too fast. [*] Towers are just boring. Power ups even more so. There is no real comboing of towers. Most of my later gameplay became trying to find where I can make a long stretch to place 2 Mass Driver towers against each other with slow vents. [*] Not enough tiles & blockers. Maybe surival is the way to go, since that has 30 waves, but campaign and quickplay have so little waves & blocks/tiles that you barely change the map or maze. By the time you've made any significant changes the map is over. [*] The game needs more talents. Completing a wave usually gives you 1-3 bonus options to pick, however 95% of the time those options are power/money/tiles/blocks, which is imo what you should get by default for just completing waves, not as bonuses. In quick play, and probably survival, you sometimes get talents, which can make significant changes and are the only slightly interesting rogue-like elements, but they are too rare and too little. In the campaign, they are part of the progression so you dont get them. [/olist] So yeah, with all that said, maybe check back after an update or two because the game needs a lot of work. If you want a good TD, hit up the old reliable youtd on an older wc3 patch before reeeeeforged broke it and play that.

Of all the TD games I've played lately, this is the deepest one. The combined aspects of building a path and managing your tile resources, gaining buffs and boons over time, deciding between towers for your build, and careful arrangement and re-arrangement of your layout, is very rewarding. Climbing the leaderboards with each game is satisfying, and I always feel like I could do just a little bit better. The visuals are good, its nice to not have a TD game with cartoony graphics and juvenile themes like Bloons TD or Kingdom Rush. The music is pretty good too, although they use a computer voice called Vocaloid to sing parts of the background music and its a little distracting hearing them yell "Hey ya ho ya hah, ho ya hey ya hay" as if the producer just tossed in some vocal intonations from a short list of basic vowel sounds. I also think the soundtrack is a little anachronistic, playing things like banjos and bongos and other tribal and earthy instruments, when... this is clearly a deep technology landscape. I don't understand why there is a banjo. Other than that, love the game.

It's a decent TD but both the towers and enemies really lack identity compared to element td. The way that elements combined led to so much more interesting results than 'generic sci-fi tower #3'. It's a shame that the developers abandoned that game to work on this one. The meta-progression feels very weak and uninteresting. I wish it changed your gameplay in more significant ways than 'get x more credits per round' and such. Something to give you more options rather than incrementally increase your power.
This TD game is a giant leap backward for Element Studios when compared to their previously released Element TD2 game.

If you're into tower defense, and you've played all the good ones, then here is yet another one. It's not great, but at least it's long, with different game modes. I'll mainly be referring to survival mode, as the campaign is horribly long and dreary, and I haven't had the chance to play co-op. I'll first say that the game is very large for its kind. The dreary campaign would take many hours to complete, and just unlocking the survival mode skill tree would likely add about 30 hours to that. However, I doubt anyone could love this game enough to complete it fully. The towers feel unbalanced, with some being essential, and some useless. Effects and upgrades are unnoticeable increments - you don't see a satisfying boost in damage or effect from an upgrade, but rather a 5% increase in damage to slowed enemies or whatever. The exceptions are weapons against shields and armor - both have no use, until they become an absolute necessity, meaning there is no choice involved in acquiring them. Visually, both towers and enemies look indistinct, making it hard to quickly assess what's going on. Unfortunately, there is no pausing the flow of the game, which would have helped with that. The menus look like placeholder graphics, and despite the dull particle effects, the game manages to slow my computer, which plays normally plays new games on ultra. 3 out of the 4 songs on the soundtrack are cool though. Despite its good points, I can't recommend Axon TD:Uprising, when there are better alternatives out there, for free, which were made more than a decade ago.

[h1]简介[/h1] 【铁壁矩阵：轴突塔防】，是一款比较新奇的塔防类游戏，45度侧视有种设计流水线工厂的感觉（幻视异形工厂2），体验还是很不错的。 [h1]背景[/h1] 主线剧情大致上就是我们的飞船被击落，遭到了怪物们的攻击，需要用有限的资源和武器合理规划，来保卫自己不受敌人迫害。 [h1]感受[/h1] 名字很直观的看出游戏的主要玩法就是塔防，模式选择上大致分为了快速游戏、战役模式、生存模式以及合作模式4种，也照顾到了一些玩家想要联机的需求，玩法上来说体验做的算是很全面了，最重要的一点是，它上架了创意工坊，相信随着时间的推移各种各样的新地图，各种美化mod，二次元mod将会推出。本作最亮点的地方是它将怪物前进的路线设置成为了可调整修改的类型，在此基础上设计布置合适的武器种类，对沿线的敌人进行进攻，还加入了连击数显示，可以更直观的看到各种武器的实际效果与攻速，更主要的是加强了视觉冲击力，玩起来比较上头，让人很想通过不断地调整以达到更好的效果，战役的关卡数也很多 ，玩起来量大管饱。画面特效上做的也算不错，几十种炮塔搭配组合，有输出的、有打控制的（制作组把同种类的炮塔都放到了同一区域，选择起来非常方便），加上各种配装，技能点的加入，那可以玩的花样就更多了，想象力越丰富玩起来越爽快，炮塔的分歧升级做的也很合适，不同种类的怪物，使用不同的分支升级会有意想不到的效果。综合考虑可以给到9分。 [h1]结语[/h1] 总的来说，【铁壁矩阵：轴突塔防】是一款极具吸引力的塔防游戏，完美结合了策略性和趣味性。其丰富多样的塔楼选择，以及逐渐提升的难度设计，使得每一局都充满了挑战与乐趣。无论你是塔防游戏的新手还是资深玩家，都能够在这里找到适合自己的玩法体验。请在无尽的可能性中，书写属于你的传奇吧。 [quote]欢迎关注鉴赏家: [url=store.steampowered.com/curator/37196866/] 稻荷窝 [/url] 只写我们喜欢的游戏 欢迎加入Steam组:[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/daohewo] 稻荷的小窝 [/url] 来一起感受游戏的乐趣 喜欢这篇评论，也是可以顺手点个赞哟[/quote]

I was having fun until just beyond the half way mark in the campaign, and then the level design changed abruptly, expecting very specific builds in order to be successful. Bad tutorialization of expected player approaches when a strategy that had been working to get all-levels completely perfect is suddenly invalidated and there is no guidance on how to do better. I went looking on youtube-- the game is not very popular and does not have a lot of videos-- and some of the early access videos that are still up show a very different level design. The "Beta" level in particular is a prime example of a huge shift from how things worked in early access to how things work now. I would have been OK if the build that was working perfectly in previous maps was successful but didn't perform as well. I would have been OK if there had been proper tutorialization or guidance on the build the specific map expected, so that you can learn the lessons the devs want the players to learn. But the decision to make me play the same map over and over and over to find a remotely viable build in the face of this level of build customization stops being fun.

One thing I miss from some of the other TD's is mazeing/routing. This game highlights it in such a great way. Not only that, but the campaign has a great sense of progression, a fun story, and gradually increases the challenge in an exciting way. I haven't explored it yet but coop is available and PvP will be soon. Lots of great features from a category that sometimes leaves you wanting more. Overall its really one of the best TD's I've played and definitely worth the price.

这是一款非常硬核的塔防类游戏，有多硬核呢，这么说吧，你在每次开局都要提前通过地图样貌规划好一整局的思路，并且要考虑到敌人的特性在合适的位置部署合适的塔防，一旦塔防的位置或者种类不合理，怪物们几乎就会全部冲到终点。并且前期你看似合理的建筑布局，到了后期你才会幡然醒悟这种布局是完全错误的，然后不得不耗费更多的资源去弥补开局带来的损失。 如果你觉得这种难度不算什么的话，那么恭喜你，你成功通过了教程的考验，并且喜提成就“你还一无所知”。当你打开快速游戏找一张地图准备大放异彩的时候，仅仅是选择界面就让您眼前一黑，你需要先从40座各具特色的建筑中选择8座、10种不同的配装选择两种才能开始游戏。 40座建筑，要想能够抵御各种怪物入侵并且平均消费的金额合理，需要花费大量精力去研究每种建筑的特性，另一方面。激活过载的时机也非常重要，想要达成完美无伤通关，仅仅依靠建筑自身的攻击是远远不够的。当然，通过实战了解每个建筑的特性最合适了，毕竟实践出真知。 从某种意义上讲，每一关的难度几乎是指数性升高，地图也大幅度复杂，因此需要规划的路线就需要更加的谨慎。另外，每轮的奖励也具有一定的肉鸽元素，选好有用的道具以及buff有时会让局势力挽狂澜。 游戏一共有5种模式可供挑选，分别是快速游戏、战役、生存、合作、pvp。遗憾的是，由于笔者身边没有合适的朋友一起游玩，因此无法体验这款游戏联机的乐趣了。不过另外三种模式已经量大管饱了，足够我们畅玩很久了，尤其是快速游戏,，一共有七大关，三种难度，如果真把这个模式的所有关卡研究明白，那么你将成为因为独断万古的塔防高手。 [quote]寻找游戏里的独特风味，发现玩法中的创意挑战 点击关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45063541/]鱼汤里的咸鱼[/url] 欢迎加入[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/YTLDXY/]鱼汤里的咸鱼群组[/url] [/quote]

Axon TD: Uprising is a tower defence game from the developers of Element TD. The player must defend an industrial planet from the Axons, robots designed for mining who have rebelled against their creators. [h1]Gameplay (high quality)[/h1] • There’s a strong focus on creating mazes to alter the path the Axons will take to your base by placing towers to block potential routes, and also by adding or removing tiles to change the layout of the map. Some missions also provide destination shifters, which allow the player to relocate the base that the Axons are trying to reach. • There are several types of Axon who will provide different challenges to the player. Healers will repair nearby Axons, spawners will create more Axons, teleporters will move further along the path when taking damage, hovercraft will fly over your towers and bypass the maze, cloakers will become temporarily invisible to your towers, disablers can temporarily deactivate nearby towers, and builders will temporarily add new tiles to the map to create a shortcut in the maze. And there are several bosses who have large health bars and more unique abilities. • You’ll start each mission with a number of lives based on the difficulty level. If an Axon reaches your base, you’ll lose some lives, with the exact number depending on the type of Axon. However, if a boss reaches the base, you’ll instantly lose the mission no matter how many lives you had remaining. If you don’t want to replay the whole mission, you can try again from the beginning of the current wave. • There are 40 different towers to choose from, which includes a mixture of single target and area of effect attacks. While many towers fire in a radius around itself, some fire straight forward in a line, while others are traps which are placed on the path and trigger when an Axon walks over it, and there are drones which follow the targeted Axon until its destroyed. • Towers can be upgraded with increased damage and special abilities which last for the rest of the mission, or overloaded which provides temporary boosts. Each tower has four upgrade options, and there are several different overloads. • At the end of each wave, the player will be able to choose between three reward options which will influence your tactics. Credits can be spent on new towers, power can be spent to upgrade or overload towers, and adds/removes will let you change the map layout. You’ll also be offered various special technologies which provide passive bonuses such as regaining lives at the end of each wave, or increasing damage dealt to Axons near the end of their path. • There are three different game modes. The story campaign features 40 missions, and each mission will have a new tower already placed on the map, which lets you test its functionality before deciding if you want to add it to your loadout in future missions. Quickplay features 21 missions, all towers are unlocked immediately and there are no story cutscenes. Survival is an endless mode which has 4 maps, and new towers will be offered randomly at the end of each wave, which means you might not always be able to use your favourites. • Some maps will ask you to defend multiple paths between different entrance portals and bases, while other maps will have Axons moving in both directions along the same path, with one groups’ starting point being the other groups’ end point. • Most maps also have pre-placed generators which will provide extra credits and power at the end of each wave, amplifiers which increase the damage of adjacent towers, and slow fields which reduce the movement speed of nearby Axons. Each item can be activated by placing a tower next to them. • There are lots of tactical options, which is a good thing most of the time because this provides variety of playing styles. However, there’s also a downside, because when you lose a mission, or lose a large number of lives in a wave, it can sometimes be difficult to understand where you’re going wrong. Is the shape of the maze wrong? Am I using the wrong towers? The wrong upgrades? Should I use overloads more often? • One mission in particular (the 4th boss mission in story mode) caused me significant problems. I was losing in early waves, even before the boss spawned, and I eventually had to drop the difficulty to easy to get past it. As I beat the first 9 missions on hard and all the other missions on normal, I feel like this one mission is probably just unbalanced. There’s a massive number of enemies incoming from 4 paths simultaneously, and even after redesigning my defences to activate all the credit generators, I felt like I didn’t have anywhere near enough funds to build an effective maze. [h1]Story (low quality)[/h1] • I didn’t like the main characters, a Human and a robot. There were too many attempted jokes which felt out of place or that I simply didn’t find funny. The rest of the story was mostly generic big corporations doing bad things. [h1]Technical (high quality)[/h1] • I’m not sure how long the story campaign took to complete, but I’ve played nearly 50 hours across all 3 game modes, which is good value. • I didn’t have any problems with bugs, crashes or framerate. • The art style is visually less interesting and colourful compared to Element TD. [h1]Recommendation[/h1] Axon TD is a fun tower defence game, which fans of the genre should enjoy, due to the wide variety of enemies, towers, and other tactical options.

Really fun and challenging game. Even as I learn more about gameplay and strategy, there is so much room to still grow and improve to beat the harder challenges. Good variety of different modes to play. Playing survival mode offers endless variety as you have to choose from the towers and boosts offered to you randomly each wave, so I doubt any two games you play will ever be the same! Playing together as 3+ players is unfortunately currently very limited in what you can play, but as 2 players you can do (I think) everything that you can do solo. You can even do the co-op maps as one player and the game will reward you double, so you essentially play as both players. This just increases the solo gameplay variety, like playing two games at once with one brain (if the map is split and each player is meant to cover a separate path). It reminds me a lot of the Sanctum games, just without the first person shooting, but with much more tower variety and more to do as a top-down-view overlord, especially with the special powers you can use during the wave in an emergency. I think it is ideal as a solo game or 2-player co-op if you have a way to voice chat.

TLDR; This is by far the best tower defense game I've ever played. I have played dozens of these types of games and finally found one that is innovative, fun and engaging. And has near infinite replay value thanks to the different game modes and map editor allowing anyone to make custom maps. In my 30 years of gaming there are rarely games that stick with me for a long time but I think Axon TD will be one of those games. I played the game for a while a couple of months ago, there were some balance changes that I didn't enjoy so I took a break. I came back and the balance is better than ever, they expanded the campaign significantly and there is a map editor that kind of reminds me of Heroes of Might and Magic 3 a little. The towers have new upgrades and overall the changes to the game are just great. It's been so long since I found a game with good and competent devs who actually significantly improve the game instead of trying to introduce money grubby "features" to milk it for as much money as possible, it feels so refreshing. Highly recommend for anyone who likes tower defense games or wants to try them. Love this game! <3

Mechanically this is a very good tower defense game and I can't deny that. It's just not that fun to play for me. The presentation is elaborate with high production values for a TD game while at the same time being very bleak, empty and soulless. For some reason they invested time and resources to render this in 3D, which is completely useless. Instead they could have invested in some more colour and pleasantness. They could have made the enemies more distinct and the weapons more varied. The whole presentation, it's all so very sterile. Maybe if everything else was perfect I would have looked past it but somehow there's also so very much and so very little at the same time. You get a big map, lots of towers to choose from and dozens of choices to go about it... but after the waves are done I always feel I haven't scratched the surface of what could have been done. That sounds like it should be a positive thing and I'm sure for many people it is. I'm constantly waiting for the game to start showing it's potential and it never feels like it does, but it's always so close. I think I should give it one more shot because any time now it's all going to click and it's going to be amazing. I'm just missing one piece of the puzzle, that's all. Maybe there is that missing piece but I've given up on finding it. I'm giving it a thumbs down but if it makes you feel better, I feel bad about it. I remember I had a very similar feeling with Element TD.

非常棒的作品，游戏灵感来自防御阵型，但是设计上更加优秀。 优点：1.教程模式非常详细，基本上涵盖了所有基础和部分进阶操作 2.4大势力的塔解锁循序渐进，每个塔的优劣势随着剧情的推进逐步给你展示和分析，不像其他TD游戏那样需要你自己摸索 3.游戏的核心玩法在于铺更长的路+更多的塔+更快的灭敌速度。这样做可以得到更高的分数。但是也不限制玩家的玩法，很多地图不需要太多塔，太长路一样轻松过关 4.过关奖励可选择性高，根据自己的流派玩法选择合适的奖励，规划适合自己技能加点和阵容搭配的选择 5.游戏不像魔兽争霸3 TD地图那样无脑堆塔，弱智玩法。而是需要合理布局，合理搭配，多钟玩法均可达成高分，无需按部就班 6.所有怪都有弱点可寻，有专门克制的塔可选。但是也无需绝对的必须使用克制对象。基础塔通过技能搭配和路线规划也可以打出比高级塔更强的伤害，清图速度和性价比。这个是此部游戏设计最好的地方，不像其他TD游戏，基础塔类只能前期用用或者直接弃用。 7.每局游戏前期的经济限制及中期的强力新敌人单位使得游戏更具挑战性，更需要提前规划能力。无论普通困难，一但前期布局OK，后期都是虐菜。 总之，这是一款很棒的TD游戏，强烈推荐

So here's my clearcut review while playing coop with a buddy. The game runs smoothly, there's a ton of content to be had here with a wide variety of towers. A great variety of missions and strategies to employ. Providing both a tech tree and your towers each with their own upgrades etc and bonuses really expand upon the gameplay and replay value. There's a wide variety of modes within the game too which is a nice touch, as most TD games only present you the campaign and maybe a survival mode but here there's both: - coop, singleplayer, Survival, PvP which definitely changes things up a bit. Now despite enjoying the game my friend and I have a few complaints. 1. Multiplayer/PvP: It's less about implementing your own unique synergies and finding a strategy that works well for you and more about employing the Meta as there are clearly some tech bonuses that're the go too and some which are to simply be ignored. 2. Solo/Coop: The developer got very lazy with unit variation; as there's an absurd amount of enemies here that merely heal or provide healing bonuses to their allies. It's expected in these games to encounter at least one medic but not several and this is turning the game into a drag dealing with nothing but medics and revival units. 3. UI/Scaling: There's unfortunately, no way to scale the interface so if you're playing on a wider monitor etc you're likely gonna see smaller text then what you would probably prefer. While this is feasible it's still annoying.

This is a very classic Tower Defense game. You have a grid to place towers on, but also gain tile pieces to expand the map with an open up mazing routes. Enemies come in a variety of forms from armored, to healing, to splitting and you get a variety of towers and upgrades to deal with them. The problem with this game is that it feels very standard and unexciting. The whole aesthetic feels kind of drab to me, and everything in the game is something we have seen before. Grid based mazing with these enemy types we have had since like 2005. Things also don't escalate much during games, with no great synergies or fun combos to pull off, just very incremental feeling improvements. I will compliment the challenge this game provides, as getting no life lost runs can be very difficult and you'll really have to counter play what the game throws at you. But sadly that alone is not enough to be fun or compelling. The art and music unfortunately is what cemented this game as generic for me. Its not much to look at or listen to. There really is not much more to say. While there is a story and campaign to go through, with characters and world building, it also was all very uninteresting to me. I never felt like I really wanted to learn or see more. I do actually recommend this game to the spreadsheet warrior type of tower defense player, that only cares about a challenge. There is not much here to really hold anyone else's attention, but if you enjoy fighting for every small quantifiable advantage and care about nothing else then you may enjoy it. But for everyone else, there are just way more creative and exciting tower defense games available in 2026.

Throwback to classic tower defense games. A great balance of mazing and smart tower placement is needed to master this game. The towers all have their roles, and the enemies ensure that you place your towers strategically. There have been a lot of great TD games recently, but I got this one due to the co-op. I have been playing co-op exclusively and it is great. Definitely recommended to anyone who got into the genre back in the Warcraft III days! Update: After continuing to play through the campaign, I must say that I am constantly impressed by the creativity and depth of this game. The levels all have great, creative routing options to work toward, the new enemies added each stage throw unique and interesting twists that require you to plan your strategies effectively, and each new tower unlocks so many possibilities. This is a fantastic and deep tower defense game that I can't recommend enough. And we haven't even tried survival or PvP mode yet. Kudos to the devs - they really understand the genre and are clearly passionate about it.

It's fairly quick to learn the basics of how this tower defense game works, but it's got a LOT of depth, tower interactions, the way sometimes the games 'in universe' tower manufactorer matters for synergies, the variety of enemy types, and the reclass freedom you have to design your own maze. This game has a TON of replayability, and the multiplayer is a blast. My only complaint is that I wish survival could be played with more than 2 players (up to four would be great)... oh, and I wish you could just 100% turn off the 'story' nonsense in campaign mode.
